based_on: City staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 106 Beverley Street under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act.
The property at 106 Beverley Street is on the west side of Beverley Street, south of Dundas Street West, in the Grange neighbourhood of downtown Toronto.
The property has a three-storey detached house that was built in 1855 for lawyer James Esten.
Staff and a heritage consultant agree that 106 Beverley Street has cultural heritage value and meets five of the provincial criteria for designation.
A property may be designated if it meets two or more of the nine provincial criteria.
Heritage designation allows City Council to review proposed changes or demolitions and enforce maintenance standards.
If there are no objections to the designation, staff recommend that City Council authorize the City Solicitor to introduce a bill to designate the property.
There are no financial impacts to the City from these recommendations.
